newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldovan President Snegur leads in election.
newsitem.headline: Moldovan President Snegur leads in election.

text.p: President Mircea Snegur has built a commanding lead in the first round of Moldova's presidential election, according to preliminary partial results released by the Central Electoral Commission on Monday.
But he was short of a 50 percent majority needed to win in the first round and will face a runoff with parliament chairman Petru Lucinschi on December 1.
The electoral commission said that with 64 percent of votes counted Snegur, a centrist who has some nationalist support, had 38 percent and Lucinschi 26 percent.
Other contenders were far behind, including Prime Minister Andrei Sangheli who gained a surprisingly poor 10 percent, trailing behind Communist Party leader Vladimir Voronin on 12 percent.
Nationalist Valeriu Matei received nine percent of the vote and the other four candidates were trailing with two percent or less.
The turnout was 67 percent, the electoral commission said.
Sunday's poll was the first multi-party presidential election in Moldova, and most experts have predicted a tight race between the president, leader of the parliament and the premier.
On Monday morning national radio broadcast Snegur's address to the Moldovan citizens with "sincere thanks for support".
"The majority of votes cast for me are a resolute rebuff to all revanchist and conservative left forces."
"We have two more weeks -- enough time to mobilise forces and win in the second round," Snegur said.
